Why: Local, non-parametric: predicts from the most similar students. Needs scaled inputs.
Captures non-linear thresholds and interactions without scaling; robust default for tabular data.
Sequential trees fit residuals; strong on tabular data but easier to overfit.
L2 penalty stabilises coefficients of correlated inputs (usage hours vs. unlocks, r = 0.96).
Interpretable additive model on all features; the main learned baseline.
L1 penalty tests whether the 100+ one-hot country/platform columns can be dropped.
One-feature rule of thumb: 'more social media, lower score'. Tests whether the other features add anything.
Predicts the training mean for everyone. Any useful model must beat it.
